newsitem.title: USA: Clinton departs on 12-day Asia-Pacific trip.
newsitem.headline: Clinton departs on 12-day Asia-Pacific trip.

text.p: President Bill Clinton departed on Friday for a brief vacation in Hawaii before visits to Australia, the Philippines and Thailand aimed at promoting U.S. economic ties with states on the Pacific rim.
The trip will include talks with leaders of China, Japan and South Korea when Clinton attends an APEC summit in Manila.

While Clinton still needs to assemble a second-term foreign policy team, with Secretary of State Warren Christopher and other Cabinet officers leaving in January, officials insisted this would not diminish the trip.

"He (Clinton) is the commander in chief, he's the principal architect of foreign policy, so the captain of the ship will be meeting with these people," said Samuel Berger, the deputy White House national security adviser.

"For this president, elevating our engagement with an Asia that is emerging in importance has been a priority in his first term and it will be, I believe, of even greater importance in his second term," Berger said.

The trip comes at a difficult time for Clinton. Not only must he find a replacement for Christopher, he is also in the process of revamping his White House staff and replacing at least five other departing Cabinet members including Defence Secretary William Perry and Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor.

But at a news conference before his departure on Friday the president shrugged off questions about the daunting task of replacing so many top advisers. He said all would taken care of in time for the newly elected Congress, which returns to work in January, to confirm the new Cabinet appointments.
"We will make timely appointments and they will be ready well in advance of the Congress beginning," he said. "I think we'll be in very good shape."
The 12-day trip is built around the fourth meeting of the leaders of the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, set to begin on Nov. 24 in the Philippines.
Before the conference, Clinton will hold private talks with Chinese President Jiang Zemin, Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and South Korean President Kim Young-sam.
Christopher visits Beijing before Clinton's meeting in Manila, underscoring U.S. interest in trying to improve relations with the communist giant.
The United States would like to revive a proposal made last spring by Clinton and Kim for four-way talks with North Korea and China on defusing tensions on the Korean peninsula.

Clinton is scheduled to leave Hawaii on Monday for a visit to Australia that includes talks with Prime Minister John Howard, an address to the Australian Parliament and a trip to the Great Barrier Reef.
"He will use the opportunity to take stock of the progress we've made toward building this Asian-Pacific community and his vision of what lies ahead," Berger said of that visit.
After the Manila conference, Clinton completes his trip with a stop in Thailand, which will have just completed parliamentary elections.
Berger said the visit was intended to provide "further proof ... that democracy is expanding in Asia just as it is elsewhere around the world."

The United States has a long history of military cooperation with Bangkok and works with Thai authorities to control the flow of drugs from the opium fields in the Golden Triangle, which includes parts of Thailand, Burma and Laos.
Clinton planned to return to Washington on Nov. 27, in order to spend the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday at home.
